cards.noteEnglish: Common word for Mexican-style pastries. French adaptation: the Spanish term is kept, treated as masculine (le pan dulce). French gloss: « pain sucré mexicain ».
Use cocinera for a woman. French adaptation: la cuisinière for a woman.

cards.supportEnglish: I want to compliment you on the breakfast.
cards.targetFrench: Je voudrais vous féliciter pour le petit-déjeuner.
cards.noteEnglish: Use felicitarla for a woman. French adaptation: vous is used whether the cook is a man or a woman; 'Je voudrais' (I would like) renders 'Quiero' (I want).

cards.supportEnglish: The coffee was delicious, just the way I like it.
cards.sourceSpanish: El café estaba delicioso, justo como me gusta.
cards.targetFrench: Le café était délicieux, exactement comme je l’aime.

cards.supportEnglish: I loved it because it was very soft.
cards.sourceSpanish: Me encantó porque estaba muy suave.
cards.targetFrench: J’ai adoré parce que c’était très moelleux.

cards.supportEnglish: Thank you very much for the service.
If I come back tomorrow, I'm going to order another one.
cards.sourceSpanish: Si regreso mañana, voy a pedir otro.
cards.targetFrench: Si je reviens demain, j’en prendrai un autre.

reader.supportEnglish: A traveler finishes her breakfast in a small café and wants to talk to the cook.
reader.sourceSpanish: Una viajera termina su desayuno en un café pequeño y quiere hablar con el cocinero.
reader.targetFrench: Une voyageuse termine son petit-déjeuner dans un petit café et veut parler au cuisinier.

reader.supportEnglish: She greets him and says: I want to compliment you on the breakfast.
reader.sourceSpanish: Ella lo saluda y dice: Quiero felicitarlo por el desayuno.
reader.targetFrench: Elle le salue et dit : « Je voudrais vous féliciter pour le petit-déjeuner. »

reader.supportEnglish: The coffee was very strong and had a delicious aroma, just the way I like it.
reader.sourceSpanish: El café estaba muy fuerte y tenía un aroma delicioso, justo como me gusta.
reader.targetFrench: « Le café était très fort et avait un arôme délicieux, exactement comme je l’aime. »
reader.noteEnglish: The traveler is still speaking (continued from line 2).

reader.supportEnglish: The sweet bread was soft inside and crunchy outside, and it wasn't too sweet.
reader.sourceSpanish: El pan dulce estaba suave por dentro y crujiente por fuera, y no era demasiado dulce.
reader.targetFrench: « Le pan dulce était moelleux à l’intérieur et croustillant à l’extérieur, et il n’était pas trop sucré. »
reader.noteEnglish: The traveler is still speaking. Pan dulce is kept in Spanish; French gloss: « pain sucré mexicain ».

reader.supportEnglish: I also loved the eggs, because they were creamy and very well seasoned.
reader.sourceSpanish: También me encantaron los huevos, porque estaban cremosos y muy bien sazonados.
reader.targetFrench: « J’ai aussi adoré les œufs, parce qu’ils étaient crémeux et très bien assaisonnés. »
reader.noteEnglish: The traveler is still speaking; her speech ends here.

reader.supportEnglish: The cook smiles and explains that the sweet bread is his grandmother's recipe.
reader.sourceSpanish: El cocinero sonríe y explica que el pan dulce es una receta de su abuela.
reader.targetFrench: Le cuisinier sourit et explique que le pan dulce est une recette de sa grand-mère.

reader.supportEnglish: The traveler tells him: If I come back tomorrow, I'm going to order another one of those.
reader.sourceSpanish: La viajera le dice: Si regreso mañana, voy a pedir otro de esos.
reader.targetFrench: La voyageuse lui dit : « Si je reviens demain, j’en prendrai un autre. »

reader.supportEnglish: Before leaving, she leaves a tip on the counter and thanks the staff for the service.
reader.sourceSpanish: Antes de salir, deja una propina en el mostrador y da las gracias al personal por la atención.
reader.targetFrench: Avant de partir, elle laisse un pourboire sur le comptoir et remercie le personnel pour le service.

reader.supportEnglish: The cook answers: Thank you very much, we're so glad you liked it.
reader.sourceSpanish: El cocinero responde: Muchas gracias, nos alegra mucho que le haya gustado.
reader.targetFrench: Le cuisinier répond : « Merci beaucoup, nous sommes ravis que cela vous ait plu. »

forms.frenchExample: Je félicite le cuisinier pour le petit-déjeuner.
forms.supportEnglish: I compliment the cook on the breakfast.
forms.explanationEnglish: Féliciter takes the person praised as its direct object, and pour introduces what you are praising.

Source note (Spanish): encantar is used like gustar: me encanta (one thing), me encantan (several things). French adaptation: with adorer, the person who loves is the subject and the thing loved is the direct object. Adorer is stronger than aimer and fits the source's enthusiasm.

forms.frenchExample: Je vous remercie beaucoup pour le service.
forms.supportEnglish: I am very grateful to you for the service.
forms.explanationEnglish: Source note (Spanish): irregular yo form, agradezco. French adaptation: remercier takes the person thanked as its direct object, and pour introduces what you are thanking them for. Vous corresponds to the source's usted (le).

forms.frenchExample: Je recommande ce café à mes amis.
forms.supportEnglish: I recommend this coffee to my friends.
forms.explanationEnglish: Source note (Spanish): stem change e to ie (except nosotros); this note concerns the Spanish verb only. In the French example, à introduces the people who receive the recommendation.

forms.frenchExample: Si je reviens demain, j’en prendrai un autre.
forms.supportEnglish: If I come back tomorrow, I'll order another one.
forms.explanationEnglish: Revenir conjugates like venir. After si, French uses the present for a real condition, and the main clause here uses the future (prendrai). French adaptation: prendre with en renders 'order another one'.

From memory, recall the French term for coffee, with its article.

Type the French for: Thank you very much for the service.

objectivesEnglish: As the traveler, compliment the breakfast with a specific detail, such as the strong coffee and its delicious aroma, the pan dulce that is soft inside and crunchy outside, or the creamy, well-seasoned eggs.
Say that if you come back tomorrow, you will order another one.
Thank the staff for the service.

notes: Private draft for editorial review only. It has had no qualified human review and is not approved or released. No audio, learner registration, progress, scoring or deployment exists for it; all 13 gates are false.

Source parity: all 18 cards and 9 reader lines keep the source English and Spanish strings verbatim, in source order, with 1-based IDs. The five verb mappings keep the source order and source English examples. Source notes on cards 3, 7 and 13 are kept verbatim at the start of noteEnglish, followed by a labelled French adaptation.

Pan dulce: the Spanish term is retained as 'le pan dulce' (masculine) in card 3 and reader lines 4 and 6, with the French gloss « pain sucré mexicain ». The earlier 'brioche' rendering is removed. A French editor should confirm the gloss wording.
Masculine agreement: line 7 now reads 'j’en prendrai un autre', agreeing with 'le pan dulce' and matching card 18 and the regresar example.

Reader lines 2-5: the traveler's speech runs across four lines. Each line carries its own balanced guillemets, so no line has an unclosed quotation, and lines 3-5 have a noteEnglish marking them as the traveler's continued speech. No narration was added to the French. A noteEnglish field was added to all reader lines for this purpose (null where unused).

Transparent French adaptations: 'Je voudrais' renders 'Quiero' (card 13, line 2); 'j’en prendrai un autre' (simple future) renders 'voy a pedir otro' and 'otro de esos' (card 18, line 7); 'C’est une recette maison ?' renders '¿Es una receta de la casa?' (card 16); 'adorer' renders 'encantar'. Editors may prefer 'Je veux' or 'je vais en prendre un autre' for closer literal parity.

Service wording: card 17, reader line 8 and the agradecer example now use 'le service' for 'atención', replacing 'votre accueil' / 'son accueil', so that they match the source English 'the service' and the Type prompt. Card 12 still lists both 'le service, l’accueil'.
Line 1 now uses 'veut parler' for 'quiere hablar', replacing 'souhaite parler'.

Modes: the field is now 'prompt'. Type, Say and Write give the card's source English; Say and Write add a short wording hint so that the exact French target is the expected answer. Hear and Say are script-only with audio pending; no audio exists. The earlier See prompt's remark about hyphenation was removed.

Forms: the earlier claims about French stem changes, the register of adorer, and regresar were removed. No French conjugation paradigms are supplied; editors should decide whether the schema requires them.
Tipping: the tip appears only as a narrative fact in reader line 8 and as vocabulary in card 9. The speaking objectives do not mention tipping, and no tipping custom is asserted.

Speaking: the learner plays the traveler and the partner plays the cook. The cook's opening line 'Bonjour ! Tout s’est bien passé ?' is an original French line written for this draft, not from the source passage, and needs editorial review. In the source, the traveler initiates the exchange.
